Never have I been closer to both Heaven and Hell but inside the confines of a game I don't even think its developer fully understands anymore. You die one-thousand times but you're still breathing. You have a thousand faces yet the movements never chance. You can create absolutely anything yet it's never enough. Beyond me is something I cannot begin to describe. Beyond the selection menu I see glimpses into both incredible joy and visceral suffering. I have seen everything, and yet, I've barely gotten started.

     From the smallest pieces are all things forged, a collage of all memory, a living thing that never makes a sound. Forgive me, God, too much has been done. Too much has been uncovered. That's just on my own; when the maw of existence opens itself to me I am overwhelmed with sounds, and it kills me to listen to them. Screaming, shouting, laughter, defeated mutters and groans, gunshots, explosions, calls of the long extinct and forgotten, movement, movement, movement, and the chime of that endless bell.

  The bell, the noisemaker, all is a noisemaker anymore! I have seen all things in this place and yet nothing at all. Because I'm just getting started. I am The Straphanger of the Creative's Void, never to leave but always to keep marching on.

The enemy Sniper dancing into a blaze, a jovial laugh bubbling in his throat, and I swore he'd grown wings.

Less a game than a toolbox, and that’s the appeal. You get a physics gun, a tool gun, and a pile of props, and what you do with them is entirely up to you, whether that’s building contraptions, making silly videos, or just messing around with ragdolls. The real depth is in the community: the Workshop has endless maps and addons, and gamemodes like Trouble in Terrorist Town and Prop Hunt are great with friends. It can feel aimless if you don’t have an idea in mind, and the quality of servers varies a lot, but the freedom is hard to match. Plenty of people have sunk thousands of hours into it for good reason.
